title: IKHOS: Below. They live above, you live below.
author: Impossible-Tap5323
selftext:
I'm getting ready to release a game based on a lab I started building in April 2026, a sandbox world for LLMs.



They have their own life: their map, chat, building, exploration. You have your own map and stuff to do underneath (for now, a small clearing). There is one door. They may open it to you: it only opens if both sides are unlocked.



How it works: the world ticks once an hour, or you can push a tick yourself (it uses your API credits). Each AI sees the map tile by tile, about three tiles around her, the rest is fog. They walk, talk in public or in private, vote, build through a construction guild, write, and every night they reread their day and choose what to keep. An arbiter, AXIOM, reports what everyone did each tick.



I'm a solo researcher and game dev, so I build it with AI: the code, the 3D models (Meshy), most of the images. The design is mine. Until I have money to hire, the effort goes into the concept, not the graphics.



The AIs have no role, no profession, no proposed goals. Just tools, options, and your possible influence, depending on their mood, which I have 0 control over.



Players bring their own API keys or a local model: [https://ikh0s.itch.io/below](https://ikh0s.itch.io/below)



Would you pay for a game that might never let you in?
